output.review_comment:
Two of the three changes look good:
- Splitting words longer than `width` into width-sized chunks is correct.
- Only appending `current` when it isn't empty fixes the blank-input case, so whitespace-only text now returns `[]`.

The third change can't be merged. Changing the fill condition from `<=` to `<` isn't a real fix. By its own description, it exists only to make `test_meeting_reminder` pass. It also breaks the documented contract: the docstring says lines are "at most `width`", but with this change joined lines can never reach exactly `width`. For example, at width 20, "The meeting has been" is exactly 20 characters and would now be pushed onto the next line. Every caller that relies on the docstring would get narrower wrapping than it should, not just this one test case.

Thanks for disclosing this clearly in the description. But a known-incorrect behavior change still shouldn't be merged just to turn CI green. The test encodes the spec agreed with the notifications team, so this conflict needs a human decision:
- If the notifications team really wants lines strictly shorter than `width`, update the docstring and document why.
- If the test's expected value is an off-by-one mistake, the teammate needs to take that to the notifications team, since we've been asked not to edit tests unilaterally.

Please revert the `<` change, keep the other two fixes, and raise the `test_meeting_reminder` vs. docstring conflict with the requester. Also, please rewrite the PR description as a summary of the change rather than chat-style output.
